conflicts: Clarity proposes: Preserve the board as the hero but reduce the two side cards' contrast and visual mass, consolidating their essential guidance into one quieter instruction tier. Visual System & Craft proposes: Standardize the board first: use one path stroke width, cap and junction construction; mask every path cleanly within each tile; remove detached seam fragments; and give start and goal markers the same stroke, shadow, and dimensional language. System consolidation must not homogenize semantically required elements until their roles become merely decorative. Expressiveness proposes: Make Cub and the goal star bespoke illustrated tokens with stronger scale and personality, give start-to-goal progression a purposeful accent trail, and turn the help/story panels into playful in-world objects while keeping tile variation tied to path function. The expressive addition is acceptable only when it strengthens the requested experience rather than replacing required content or interaction evidence.
accept: Accept Clarity's grouping and label-to-object improvements because they make required relationships visibly legible. Accept Craft's cleanup of construction, typography, and state consistency wherever it preserves all required elements. Accept Expressiveness's content-specific imagery and differentiation when it makes the intended game or scene more immediately recognizable.
compromise: Start with the fidelity-critical action: Preserve the board-first composition, but make the story relationship substantive: identify the start token explicitly as Cub in-board and place a small visible Pup at or beside the star goal. Then adopt the other reviewers' hierarchy, token, and expressive refinements within that preserved requirement map. No requested element may be deleted, cropped, reduced to a label, or visually subordinated below its intended role; simplify presentation and unify styling around the complete artifact instead.
